correctness.rationale: Rayleigh–Ritz plane minimization of Q has symmetric compression [[e,√e c],[√e c,D]], so new error is its smaller eigenvalue and normalized multiplier has rationalized form 2(D−c²)/(e+D+sqrt((D−e)²+4ec²)). Coupled Gaussian tangent at e→0 gives (Z₂²+⋯+Z_m²)/(Z₁²+⋯+Z_m²), Beta((m−1)/2,1/2). Multipliers are bounded in [0,1]; O(r)×O(m) symmetry makes conditional kernels functions of e only. Since e_{j+1}≤e_j, uniform small-e convergence and induction yield k independent beta limits at each fixed horizon and the gamma-moment formula. Independent Gaussian calculations checked mean and second moments in three codimensions (20,000 samples each), not a substitute for the limit proof.
residual_risks: Random finite samples cannot establish all-dimensional beta weak convergence or iid products; these require the Gaussian coupling and kernel argument.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS: Bresch–Melnyk global linear convergence with a positive top spectral gap treats a simple leading eigenvalue, not a rank-r≥2 repeated leading eigenspace. Earlier random-plane algorithm and generalized Rayleigh quotient papers give method and general rates but no identified local beta multiplier law or fixed-k independent product. Similar beta errors in Gaussian Krylov/linear-system algorithms arise under different projection kernels and do not prove this Rayleigh–Ritz claim. Full inaccessible relevant primary text remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Full arXiv manuscripts for the exact prior random-plane method and generalized multiplicity have not all been inspected; an equivalent local law under different language remains possible.

value.rationale: Exact local beta multiplier law is a natural stochastic refinement of mean convergence for random-plane eigenvalue ascent when the top eigenvalue is degenerate, beyond existing simple-top spectral-gap analysis. Rank-independent beta shape, all moments and fixed-horizon iid product supply precise, reusable error-distribution information; motivated structural theorem, not a chosen finite test.
residual_risks: This gives only fixed-horizon local information, not a universal asymptotic convergence theorem.

limitations: Only real two-eigenvalue H=λ_-I+ΔP, r≥2,m≥2, tangent plane uniform, fixed horizon k, error ε→0; not general multi-level matrix or uniform-in-time rate. Primary full-text gaps limit historical priority confidence.
